Ava (Finance Ops): :loudspeaker: Quick policy update — effective immediately we are placing a temporary monthly p-card spend cap of $5,000 per card across the company. This is to address a recent uptick in anomalous vendor activity and to align Q2 discretionary spend to the updated forecast. The cap will remain in place through 2026-04-15 unless we notify otherwise.

Ava (Finance Ops): What this means: any single-card charges that would push a card over $5k in a calendar month will be declined. If you have planned vendor spend that will exceed this, please request an exception via the procurement exception form (link below). Exceptions are for business-critical purchases only and require FP&A + Procurement signoff.

Ava (Finance Ops): Links — Confluence FAQ: https://redwood.internal/confluence/pcard-temporary-cap (see "exceptions" section). Exception request form: https://redwood.internal/forms/procurement-exception. For urgent vendor payments tied to live customer incidents, add "INCIDENT" to the form subject and tag @Sam (Procurement).

Ava (Finance Ops): Cardholders please: 1) review upcoming scheduled charges, 2) pause any non-critical subscriptions, and 3) route any large purchases through the form. We expect to lift the cap after the vendor activity review. :white_check_mark:

Diego (FP&A): Heads up — teams should audit planned vendor spend for the next 30 days and flag reprioritized items to FP&A by EOD tomorrow. We'll triage exceptions against Q2 commitments.

Lina (Eng Manager): Quick Q — for Dedicated infra burst credits already approved, if we hit the cap will that block capacity reservations?

Sam (Procurement): Lina — if you already have an existing reserved capacity contract or approved burst credit, that spend is grandfathered. Only new single-card charges exceeding $5k/month are affected. If autoscaling might push you over, submit the exception form with the contract reference and cc procurement@redwood.com.

Lina (Eng Manager): Got it, will submit. Thanks.

Diego (FP&A): Note: approved exceptions will go to a short cross-functional review (FP&A + Procurement + Finance Ops). Expect 24–48h turnaround for standard requests. If it's customer-impacting mark "EXPEDITE" and we'll prioritize.

Accounting Bot: Automated note — card reconciliation schedule unchanged. Please attach receipts in Concur within 5 business days to avoid holds.

Ava (Finance Ops): Apologies for the disruption — we know temporary caps are annoying, but this helps protect customer and company funds while we complete the vendor review. DM me for edge cases. :pray:
